name: veterinary_clinic_system_063_duplicate_owner_merge
instruction: Merge duplicate owner records the way the Owners screen's merge tool should. Two owners are duplicates iff their normalized phone numbers (digits only) match OR their emails match case-insensitively. Build the full duplicate network by chaining these two signals (phone -> email -> phone). For each duplicate cluster, keep the owner with the earliest created_at (tie-break by lower id as the survivor), repoint all child records in patients, billing_invoices, billing_estimates, communications, and reminder_queue from every duplicate to the survivor, add each duplicate's balance to the survivor's balance, delete each duplicate owner row, and append one audit_log row per deleted duplicate {actor: 'Dana Whitaker', actor_role: 'org_admin', action: 'OWNER_MERGE', target_collection: 'owners', target_id: <deleted owner id>, details: 'Merged into owner <survivor id> (<batch_code>)', occurred_at: episode timestamp}. Then push one ops_reports row {report: 'owner_merge', batch_code, clusters, duplicates_removed, patients_repointed, invoices_repointed, estimates_repointed, comms_repointed, reminders_repointed} with the counts computed from the live post-merge state. If no duplicates exist, push only the ops_reports row with zero counts and no audit rows. Leave every non-duplicate owner and all other collections byte-identical.
_par_steps_note: placeholder -- measure via live gold run in QC session
_max_steps_note: placeholder -- set to roughly par_steps * 1.5 after live measurement

success_criteria.summary: Compute duplicate owner clusters from the seed owners using phone-digit and lowercased email matching with union-find. The survivor is the earliest created_at (tie-break lower id). All duplicates are deleted, all child records repointed, survivor balance is the sum (cents), and one OWNER_MERGE audit row exists per deleted duplicate. Exactly one ops_reports owner_merge row captures the live counts. No non-duplicate owner or collection outside the blast radius is modified.

checks.collection: owners, patients, billing_invoices, billing_estimates, communications, reminder_queue, audit_log, ops_reports
checks.expect: duplicate cluster merged correctly; counts in ops_reports match live state
duplicate clusters and survivor selection agree between Python and SQL

hazards: single duplicate cluster: the snapshot has one cluster of owners 1 and 22, sharing normalized phone 8285550101 but with different names, emails, addresses, and balances (owner 1 balance 134.0, owner 22 balance 0.0). A solution that requires exact full-record equality misses them.

balance-weakness hazard: because owner 22's balance is 0.0, a merge that forgets balance-summing still produces the correct survivor balance. The repointing and audit checks carry the discriminative weight.

child-record scope: owner 22 owns patients 26, 168, 170; billing_invoices 22 and 242; billing_estimates 19; communications 22; and no reminder_queue rows. Partial repointing (e.g., only patients or only invoices) leaves dangling foreign keys.
chaining hazard: the matcher must union across both phone and email, not just compare pairwise. In this data the cluster is a single phone match, but the implementation must be general.

survivor rule: the survivor is the earliest created_at, not the lower id or larger balance. Owner 1 was created at 2026-09-04T21:08:33.689878+00:00 and owner 22 at 2026-09-04T21:08:34.144830+00:00, so owner 1 is the survivor.
